newsitem.title: GERMANY: Commerzbank says it not takeover target.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank says it not takeover target.

text.p: Commerzbank chief executive Martin Kohlhaussen said on Thursday that the bank was not a takeover candidate, but was rather itself seeking acquisitions.

Speaking to reporters after a ceremony to mark the opening of a new wing at the bank's headquarters in Frankfurt, Kohlhaussen also said that the bank's first half profits should allow it to post good results for the full year.
"We've have never been alone, but we have always been independent," Kohlhaussen said.
"We know what we want. We are not a takeover candidate. We are rather someone who is actively looking for other candidates," he said.
Kohlhaussen did not specify where Commerzbank might be interested in a takeover, but downplayed the idea of buying another bank in Europe outside Germany.
Kohlhaussen said that there had been "no great success story" in European cross-border deals in the banking sector in recent times.

A spokesman for the bank later said that Commerzbank had already taken over several smaller units in past years, adding that asset management appeared at any rate not to be a topic for further consideration.
Kohlhaussen also said that he was pleased with the bank's performance in the first half of 1997, when operating profit rose by 23.2 percent.
"We have every reason to expect a very decent result for the full year," he said.
